Bundle branch block is a condition in which there is a delay or blockage along the pathway that electrical impulses travel to make the heart beat. The delay or blockage can occur on the pathway that sends electrical impulses to the left or the right side of the ventricles. In left bundle branch block, impulses travel first via the right bundle branch to the right ventricle and then to the left ventricle via the septum, reversing septal activation and eliminating lateral Q waves. The overall depolarisation vector from the right to left ventricle produces tall R waves in lateral leads and deep S waves in right precordial leads, and the delay to the left ventricle extends the QRS duration to at least 120 ms.
Bundle branch block sometimes makes it harder for the heart to pump blood to the rest of the body and may not need treatment. When treatment is needed, it involves managing the underlying health condition, such as heart disease, that caused bundle branch block. Most people with bundle branch block do not have symptoms; rarely, fainting or feeling as if you are going to faint can occur.

Coronary artery disease is a common type of heart disease that affects the coronary arteries. In CAD, there is reduced blood flow to the heart muscle. A buildup of fats, cholesterol and other substances in and on the artery walls, called atherosclerosis, usually causes coronary artery disease. The buildup, called plaque, makes the arteries narrow. Coronary artery disease often develops over many years. Symptoms are from the lack of blood flow to the heart. A complete blockage of blood flow can cause a heart attack.
Treatment for coronary artery disease may include medicines and surgery. Eating a nutritious diet, getting regular exercise and not smoking can help prevent coronary artery disease and the conditions that can cause it. Coronary artery disease also may be called coronary heart disease.

Cardiomyopathy is a disease of the heart muscle that makes it harder for the heart to pump blood to the rest of the body and can lead to symptoms of heart failure. It can also lead to other serious heart conditions. There are various types, including dilated, hypertrophic, and restrictive cardiomyopathy. +Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is one of the most common inherited cardiac disorders, with prevalence around 1 in 500 people and annual mortality around 1 to 2 percent. It is produced by mutations in multiple genes coding for sarcomeric proteins and is primarily autosomal dominant with variable penetrance. Dilated cardiomyopathy is characterized by ventricular dilatation and global myocardial dysfunction with ejection fraction less than 40 percent. Restrictive cardiomyopathy is the least common form and occurs in advanced stages of infiltrative disease such as haemochromatosis, amyloidosis, or sarcoidosis.
